digest.component_or_area: snapshot store garbage collection and janitor
propositions: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host that resolves attested gates populates the snapshot store without ever reclaiming it, causing unbounded growth.

An operation-linked GC trigger must avoid long-lock pitfalls by using a near-free O(1) in-process check on the gate-resolution tail, with heavy GC work running in a detached child process under the snapshot store's own gc flock.
The trigger mechanism uses stamp and lock sidecars keyed on the per-host snapshot store root, enabling single-flight semantics and harmless overlap with the review-bot's resident janitor.

The trigger is called on the tail of resolve_gate_handle for attested handles only, performs one stat of the gc/last-pass.stamp file against the janitor interval_seconds cadence, and never raises into the gate operation.

A detached child process runs the existing run_gc policy with a stamped worker.lock sidecar and durable cwd anchored at the snapshot store root, records the pass only if run_gc completes successfully, and respects existing lock state via stamped_file_is_stale adjudication.

The design is operation-linked and in-process with no dependency on CI providers, cron, or daemons, and is tested with RED-first unit tests covering trigger firing, O(1) quiet path, single-flight contention, and end-to-end reclamation on a simulated non-review-bot host.
